title: Geert's journey, April 1943 – September 1947
note: Lines join the places in the order the records give; they are not the roads or railways he travelled. Positions are the towns, not exact addresses.

steps.text: Refuses to arrest Jews and goes into hiding, first at an address in Rotterdam.
Hides with H. Wiggers at the farm Plak-an near Winterswijk.
A year on Hendrik Satter's farm as “Oom Geert”, helping people in hiding and Allied airmen. He spends some weeks of it with relatives in Friesland.
Arrested at the farm. The truck takes the prisoners to Avegoor, where they are stripped: “Greydanus was in bad shape”.
Taken on to the SD (security police) building in Arnhem.
Held in Kamp Vught and tortured in its bunker, cells 117 and 93.
Sent by train with 15 others to the prison in Kleve, just over the German border.
Registered at Buchenwald concentration camp and put in the overcrowded “Little Camp”.
One of the 100 men who set up the Niederorschel subcamp, working 12-hour days for Langenwerke AG.
Death march back to Buchenwald: 527 set out and 425 arrive; the fate of the rest is unknown. US troops liberate Buchenwald on 11 April.
Reaches the reception centre in Eindhoven and sends word to Johanna: “Am well and healthy.”
Home in Rotterdam, “unrecognisable”. Back at work with the police two days later.
Sails for Canada with his family on the Tabinta. He works as a farm labourer in Ontario, later farms near Clinton, and leaves the farm when he falls ill in 1964.
